summary.text: Chris Royal is the Libertarian Party nominee for Texas's 34th District. He is an Army veteran, attorney, and retired teacher who moved to the Rio Grande Valley in 1993 and has run for this seat before as an independent. In his 2024 Candidate Connection survey, he said he is running to reduce federal spending and have existing immigration laws enforced.

paragraphs.text: Born in Kokomo, Indiana; says his family moved to Springfield, Missouri, when he was 12, where his father ran a restaurant and he worked.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Southwest Missouri State University in 1982 (he says in philosophy, with a minor in ancient history).

Served in the U.S. Army from 1982 to 1990, including at the Pentagon and with the 1st Infantry Division at Fort Riley, Kansas, and says he was called up for Operation Desert Storm and served at Fort McPherson, Georgia.
Earned a J.D. from the Kansas City School of Law in 1990, according to his survey.

Says he spent a year in Arkansas teaching himself C++ and writing a real estate textbook. Ballotpedia lists his career experience as teacher, lawyer, real estate textbook author, computer programmer, and restaurateur.
Moved permanently to the Rio Grande Valley in 1993, holding jobs in the legal, title, and teaching fields, and retired from teaching in 2024, according to his survey.

Ran for this seat as an independent in 2022, receiving 4,079 votes (3.0%). Ballotpedia lists him as a withdrawn or disqualified independent candidate in 2024, and he is the Libertarian nominee in 2026 after the party's March 21, 2026 convention.
According to his survey, he is married with two children and attends Holy Family Catholic Church in Brownsville.
